questions.stem: Which of the following is a well-formed formula?
questions.explanation: A well-formed formula must use parentheses to indicate the order of operations. Option \( (p \land (q \lor \lnot r)) \) correctly uses parentheses to group the operations.

distractorRationale.a: This lacks parentheses to group operations correctly.
distractorRationale.c: The connective \( \land \) is not used with two operands.
distractorRationale.d: The formula is not properly grouped with parentheses.

questions.stem: How many different valuations exist for a propositional formula with 3 variables?
questions.explanation: For a formula with 3 variables, each variable can be either true or false, leading to \( 2^3 = 8 \) different possible valuations.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a valid formula is true?

options.text: It is true under at least one valuation.
It is true under all valuations.
It is false under all valuations.
It is false under at least one valuation.

questions.explanation: A valid formula is one that is true under every possible valuation, which is the definition given in option b.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a satisfiable formula, not a valid one.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between a satisfiable formula and a valid formula in propositional logic.
markingGuide: A satisfiable formula is true under at least one valuation.
A valid formula is true under all possible valuations.
Examples of each type of formula.
questions.explanation: A satisfiable formula is one that can be true for some valuations, whereas a valid formula is true for every valuation. For example, \( p \lor \lnot p \) is valid as it is always true, while \( p \land q \) is satisfiable if both \( p \) and \( q \) are true.

questions.stem: Given the formula \( (p \land q) \lor r \), how many valuations make it true if \( p \) and \( q \) are both true?
questions.explanation: If \( p \) and \( q \) are both true, \( (p \land q) \) is true. Therefore, \( (p \land q) \lor r \) is true regardless of the truth value of \( r \), leading to 4 possible valuations for \( r \).

questions.stem: Which of the following formulae is unsatisfiable?
questions.explanation: The formula \( p \land \lnot p \) is unsatisfiable because it requires \( p \) to be both true and false simultaneously, which is impossible.

distractorRationale.b: This is a tautology, always true.
distractorRationale.c: This is satisfiable if both \( p \) and \( q \) are true.
distractorRationale.d: This is satisfiable if either \( p \) or \( q \) is true.

markingGuide: Identify the possible valuations of \( p, q, \) and \( r \).

questions.stem: If a formula is unsatisfiable, what can be said about its validity?

options.text: It is both valid and satisfiable.

questions.explanation: An unsatisfiable formula cannot be valid because it is not true under any valuation. Validity requires truth under all valuations.

distractorRationale.a: A valid formula must be true under all valuations, not unsatisfiable.
distractorRationale.c: Unsatisfiable means it cannot be true under any valuation.
distractorRationale.d: A formula cannot be both valid and unsatisfiable.
